summary: Brooke Schedneck is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the doctoral supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bror Fredrik Tiliander (1896–1990) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Lund University (~1916–1920) under Helmer Smith and completed his PhD at Uppsala University (~1968–1974).

Bruce B. Lawrence (born 1941) is a religious studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Fay School, Princeton University (~1962–1964), and Episcopal Divinity School (~1964–1967), he served as Professor at Duke University (~1971–2014), where he became Marcus Humanities Distinguished Professor Emeritus in 2014.

Bruce Cameron Hall is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980 and served as Assistant Editor at the College of William & Mary (attested 1987).

Bruce Charles Williams is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He was educated under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.

Bruce Chilton (born 1949) is a religious studies scholar. He studied at St John's College (~1975–1979) and held posts at Yale University (~1985–1987) and Bard College, where he became Director around 1987.

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College (1978) and earned his PhD at Columbia University (attested 1983) under Alex Wayman, having also studied under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer (born 1940) studied at the University of Sydney (~1959–1963) and University of Manchester (~1964–1969). A religious studies scholar, he held positions at Adelaide (~1973–1985), UCL (~1985–1999), Bergen (~1999–2015), Gothenburg, and James Cook University.

Bruce Lincoln (born 1948) studied at Haverford and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1970–1976 under Mircea Eliade). A religious studies and Iranian specialist, he taught at the University of Minnesota (1976–1994) and Chicago (~1995 onward).

Bruce M. Knauft (born 1954) studied at the University of Michigan (~1977–1983). Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies among other fields, he joined Emory University around 1985 as Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology.

Bruce M. Sullivan (born 1951) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Chicago (PhD 1976–1984), working under J. A. B. van Buitenen (~1975–1979), and served as Professor Emeritus at Northern Arizona University (~1988).

Bruce Matthews (born 1941) is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who did graduate work at McMaster University (~1968–1974). He held posts at the University of Ceylon (~1971–1973) and Acadia University (~1976–2006) as Professor of Comparative Religion.

Bruce McCoy Owens is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and served as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens (1935–2023) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at EFEO (1969), KU Leuven (1972–1977), the French Institute of Pondicherry (1977), and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1986).
Bruno Galasek is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2016) under the supervision of Konrad Klaus.

Bruno Liebich (1862–1939), an Indologist and linguist, earned his doctorate at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn and habilitated at Breslau. He held teaching posts at Breslau (1892; 1921–1928) and Heidelberg University (1912; ~1915–1928).

Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian studies. He studied at Leipzig, Jena, and Tübingen, learning under Rudolf von Roth and Ernst Windisch, and served as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1878–1919).

Bruno Meissner (1868–1947) was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Leipzig (~1888–1889) and Strasbourg (~1891–1892). He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (~1904–1920) and Frederick William / Humboldt University of Berlin (~1920–1936).

Bruno Petzold (1873–1949), a Buddhist and Japanese studies scholar, studied at Leipzig and Berlin, later learning from Daito Shimaji and Shinsho Hanayama. He taught at First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University (~1921–1925), Seikei High School (~1928–1944), and Rissho University.

Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a scholar of Sinology who studied under August Conrady (~1910–1919). He founded Asia Major in 1923 and worked as an editor (Verlagslektor) at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).
